questions.subject: h2-physics
questions.stemText: A toy, of mass 0.22 kg, is released from rest on a smooth curved surface as shown. [Diagram: toy at the top of a smooth curved ramp, 40 cm above the flat bottom; the ramp levels out and leads to a horizontal spring fixed at the end.] It slides down the curved surface through a vertical distance of 40 cm and strikes a spring of force constant $350\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-1}}$, and compresses it a distance $x$ before coming to rest momentarily. Assuming no energy loss, what is the value of $x$? A $4.9\times10^{-3}$ m B $7.2\times10^{-3}$ m C $2.2\times10^{-2}$ m D $7.0\times10^{-2}$ m

questions.difficultyReason: Single energy-conservation equation linking GPE to elastic PE.
questions.misconception: Forgetting to square-root or forgetting the factor of 1/2 in elastic PE

explanation.body:
All the gravitational PE lost becomes elastic PE in the spring (smooth surface, no losses):

$mgh = \tfrac12 kx^2 \Rightarrow x = \sqrt{\dfrac{2mgh}{k}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2(0.22)(9.81)(0.40)}{350}} = 7.0\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{m}$.

perOption.A: This is $x^2 = 4.9\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^2}$; the square root was not taken.
perOption.B: Too small; comes from mishandling the units or the energy equation (e.g. using $h$ in cm wrongly or dropping a factor).
perOption.C: Too small; results from an algebra slip in rearranging $\tfrac12 kx^2 = mgh$.
